figure: Figure 26.2 — Pattern Application Diagram (Pattern-Measurement-Feedback Loop on the capstone scenario)
issue: The figure's DERIVED and PATTERNS box contents cannot be reconciled with the visible mini-case prose on p. 431; either the figure overstates what the worked example derives/applies, or the prose under-states it. Steps 2–3 (pp. 432–433 / printed 412–413) were NOT in this batch and must be checked.
evidence: Box 2 reads 'DERIVED — decode bandwidth-bound (low-batch regime)', but the mini-case method output on PDF 431 / printed 411 reads: 'applies the §26.2.1 method (locate the dominant constraint: tail latency/queuing under the p99 ≤ 800 ms TTFT target), which motivates evaluating the semantic response cache (Pattern B) and the circuit breaker (Pattern C).' The figure names a resource regime (decode bandwidth) where the prose names an SLO-level constraint (tail latency/queueing), and the causal chain linking them (bandwidth-bound low-batch decode → saturation → queue growth → tail) appears in neither the figure nor the visible text. Additionally, box 3 lists 'A · Inference Sharding' alongside B and C, while the visible mini-case text (Steps 0–1, PDF 431) motivates only Patterns B and C; no application of Pattern A is visible in this batch. Secondary mismatch: box 1's 'scenario TTFT p99 ~450 ms' is the pre-intervention baseline (consistent with Step 1's 320+80+50 = 450 ms and with the p. 414 takeaway '~44% vs the ~450 ms uncached baseline'), but the loop's 'feedback / adjust + pick pattern' return edge terminates at this same 450 ms box, so a reader may read 450 ms as the post-pattern state rather than the assumption being revised.
root_cause: The diagram compresses a two-level derivation (resource regime vs SLO-binding constraint) into one DERIVED box and lists the chapter's full pattern set rather than the subset the capstone actually applies, without a caption note establishing either relationship.
correction: Either (a) revise box 2 to name the constraint the worked example actually derives (e.g., 'low-batch decode is bandwidth-bound → queueing binds the p99 TTFT SLO') or add a caption sentence making the two-level chain explicit; and (b) restrict box 3 to the patterns the capstone applies, or state in the caption which of A/B/C are exercised in Steps 2–3; and (c) consider marking box 1 as 'baseline (pre-pattern)' so the 450 ms assumption is not read as the loop's output.
acceptance_test: Re-read pp. 432–433 (printed 412–413): if Step 2 does not explicitly derive 'decode bandwidth-bound' and connect it to the queueing/tail constraint before pattern selection, or if Step 3 does not apply Pattern A, then the figure (or its caption) is revised so box 2 and box 3 match the worked example exactly; afterwards, a reader comparing p. 431, pp. 432–433, and Fig  26.2 must find one identical named dominant constraint and one identical applied-pattern set.

figure: Figure 26.1 — Workload fingerprints on the six axes
issue: The in-figure title contains editorial meta-commentary — '(grouped bars, not radar)' — that is meaningless to a first-time reader, and the title otherwise near-duplicates the caption verbatim.
evidence: In-figure title: 'Workload fingerprints on six axes (grouped bars, not radar)'. Caption: 'FIGURE 26.1: Workload fingerprints on the six axes.' The word 'radar' appears nowhere in the visible text of pp. 424–425 (the provenance note on PDF 424 / printed 404 discusses axes and authored 0–1 scores but never mentions a radar chart), so the parenthetical reads as a note to a designer/reviewer that survived into the built PDF rather than reader-facing content.
root_cause: Production/review-response note left embedded in the figure title; title and caption carry the same information with no division of labor.
correction: Replace the title with reader-facing content (e.g., 'Workload fingerprints on six axes (authored intensity, 0–1)') and let the caption carry the explanatory load ('Grouped bars; compare within an axis, not across axes'), removing the chart-type meta-commentary.

figure: Figure 25.1 — The Anatomy of an Architecture Decision Record
issue: The supersession arrow is drawn from the bottom of the ADR-001 field stack (below the Alternatives box) rather than from the Consequences box it names, and the figure label asserts a relation the caption hedges.
evidence: The dashed red arrow is labeled 'consequences of ADR-001 become the context of ADR-002' but visually originates beneath the entire five-field stack (at/below the 'Alternatives / rejected options' box), not at the 'Consequences / the effects' box. The caption states the relation hedged and scoped: 'the Consequences of ADR-001 may become part of the Context of ADR-002', whereas the figure label states 'become the context' (unhedged, whole-field). The figure's whole point is the consequences→context handoff, so the drawn anchor is the semantic payload of the diagram.
root_cause: Arrow anchored to the record as a unit instead of to the specific field the label references; label wording simplified relative to the caption.
correction: Anchor the arrow's origin at the Consequences box (or draw a short connector from that box to the arrow), and align the label with the caption's hedged phrasing (e.g., 'consequences of ADR-001 feed the context of ADR-002'), keeping the [ILLUSTRATIVE] scope intact.
acceptance_test: On the rebuilt page, the arrow's top endpoint is level with the 'Consequences' box, and the figure label and caption express the same modality (both hedged or both definite); grayscale print of p. 395 still distinguishes ADR-001 from ADR-002 via the '(superseded)' / '(new — supersedes ADR-001)' text, which it currently does.
